Question B-003-005-008.

Why the correct answer is right: The beat frequency oscillator (BFO) supplies a local reference that mixes with the intermediate frequency (IF) in the product detector so single sideband (SSB) or continuous wave (CW) information becomes audio.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It is mixed with the incoming signal to produce the intermediate frequency": Mixing with the incoming radio-frequency (RF) to make IF is the local oscillator's job earlier in the receiver.
- sourceIndex 2: "It drives the automatic gain control circuit to maintain a constant audio level": Automatic gain control (AGC) uses detected signal information to control gain. The BFO is not an AGC drive source.
- sourceIndex 3: "It is fed to the receiver input to provide band edge markers": Receiver band-edge markers are supplied by a marker generator or calibrator. The BFO stays near the product detector to provide an audio-recovery reference.
